bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: William S. (Bill) Moody joined the staff of the Rockefeller Brothers Fund (RBF) in 1968 and served as a program officer until his retirement in 2007.

Born in 1939, Moody grew up in Michigan, studied at Northwestern University, and received his J.D. degree from the University of Michigan Law School. Moody developed an early interest in international affairs. In the summer of 1956, he lived in Germany as an American Field Service (AFS) exchange student, and, as a college student, Moody spent his junior year abroad at the University of Geneva and its Graduate Institute for International Studies. In the years prior to his joining the RBF, Moody took a leave from his law firm and spent a postgraduate year studying international law at the Institute for European Studies, Free University of Brussels, from which he received a licence speciale.

Moody's work with the RBF's International Program focused initially on Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean. From the mid-1980s to the year 2000, Moody was program officer for Central and Eastern Europe, where he worked to promote sustainable development, community revitalization, and the growth of civil society. From 2001 until 2007, Moody headed the RBF's Western Balkans program, where, in addition to sustainable development and civil society projects, he worked to foster inter-ethnic communication, improve government programs and transparency, and achieve and support a "final status" for Kosovo.
On his retirement from the RBF in 2007, Moody undertook a memoirs project. His Staying the Course, a reflective review of his forty years of grantmaking at the RBF, was published in 2014.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The William S. Moody (WSM) papers document his "forty-year" career (1968-2007) as a program officer for the Rockefeller Brothers Fund (RBF). As an associate in the International Program and later program head, Moody worked on projects in Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean in the 1970s-1980s. He headed the RBF's programs in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) in the 1980s-2000s and in the Western Balkans, from 2000-2007.

WSM's papers relate to his work in these program areas - particularly his meetings, travels, correspondence, and reports. While the collection includes grant lists, dockets, and some program reviews, the files provide little information on specific grants or grantees (related grant files are found in the RBF records, Projects, RG 3).

The collection also documents other aspects of WSM's work, including participation on committees, program reports, correspondence with Rockefeller family members, presentations and talks, and service on outside or related boards. Series 8, British Virgin Islands (BVI), documents WSM's work on behalf of Laurance S. Rockefeller to broker the transfer of his Sandy Cay preserve to the BVI National Park Trust.
Other series include WSM's general correspondence files, and records relating to the preparation and publication of his memoirs.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: The Rockefeller Brothers Fund records provide a fuller context for William S. Moody's work as a program officer. See particularly the Board of Trustees materials in RG 1, Series 1; the Presidents' papers in RG 2, Series 1 (William M. Dietel) and Series 2 (Colin G. Campbell); and the Projects or Grant files in RG 3, multiple series.

The Grant files in particular may provide insight into organizations active in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) but for which detailed information is lacking in the Moody papers. Trip files and Board-related files in the Presidents' papers should also supplement or complete records found in this collection.

The series contains overviews of RBF grantmaking, trip reports, notes and memos on meetings and visits, and some conference materials. scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 2, Central and Eastern Europe, documents WSM's work on behalf of the RBF in the former Eastern Bloc countries of Europe, from the mid-1980s to the early 2000s. In 1983-1984, the RBF launched its "One World" program, focused on Sustainable Resource Use and Security (which translated to support for civil society organizations and democratic practice). In this period of transition in CEE, Poland, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia, as well as the Soviet Union, presented new opportunities for dialogue, educational exchanges, and collaboration.

The CEE series contains grant lists, background and program-planning materials, program reviews, conference reports, and topical files on foundations, civil society organizations and NGOs, democracy and governance, education, management training, community revitalization, transportation, environment, and sustainable development. While projects are often well documented, information on individual NGOs can be elusive. Documentation on some of these local and international nonprofit organizations may be found in broader program and grantmaking files at the start of this series, or in the "CEE Documents and Reports" folders (in box 4).

WSM regularly kept notes on his meetings with individuals and organizations. His notes, sometimes along with correspondence and reports, are found in the Trip files (in Series 3) especially, but are also found in various conference or topical files.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Foundation for the Development of Polish Agriculture (FDPA), which launched in February 1988, was an independent foundation established to provide practical assistance to Polish farmers and the agricultural sector. As the first such foundation in a communist country, its creation involved research and planning and extensive negotiation with the Polish government over its legal framework and charter.

FDPA projects helped farmers expand production and exports, which created revenues that allowed the FDPA in turn to expand its outreach. Programs included, among others, micro-lending (and support for women's rural enterprises) and efforts to create rural employment and to promote rural tourism.

The FDPA series includes two sets of "History" files; general files, which include Board correspondence and various proposals and reports; and records of Board Meetings for 1993-2006, with some gaps. There is also one file on the American Trust for Agriculture in Poland (ATAP, a U.S. nonprofit founded to assist in the launch of the FDPA).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE Trust) came into being in the late 1990s-2000, as foundations active in CEE contemplated possible exit strategies from the region. In 1997, WSM proposed the creation of a partnership to provide for a coordinated long-term support of civil society organizations in CEE. Between 1998-1999, six donor foundations (the Ford Foundation, German Marshall Fund, Charles Stewart Mott Foundation, Open Society Institute, Rockefeller Brothers Fund, plus Atlantic Philanthropies) together pledged $60 million to fund a Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe.

With a mission to develop and support the long-term stability of civil society organizations, the CEE Trust was established in 2000 and operated through 2012 in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia.
The records document in particular the complicated process of creating the Trust and the first several years of its operation.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: WSM's Correspondence series consists of General Correspondence, arranged chronologically, 1984-2014; a set of Chronological Files, for 1988 only; a folder of Personal and Professional Correspondence, 1989-2002, plus two folders of Personal Papers, 1975-2007; and a small set of correspondence with Colleagues and Associates (12 folders).

General Correspondence is the largest component. As its name implies, it is general in nature, including a mix of letters, announcements, proposals, articles, requests, and solicitations. In a few cases, where there is a more extended correspondence with an individual, we have arranged it alphabetically at the end of the General Correspondence.

WSM's sabbatical in 1987 slightly interrupts the run of General Correspondence. In addition to the correspondence file for 1987, the series also includes a Trip Diary for 1987 and related notes. Finally, there is an additional folder of correspondence, 1984-1987, marked for post-sabbatical "follow-up."

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Note in file indicates that it contains "Correspondence to follow up" as of October 25, 1987 (i.e., following WSM's 1987 sabbatical year).
